title: Figures 2.1-2.2: Hirsch Ion-Injection IEC Device and Neutron Output vs Applied Potential
description: Figure 2.1, 'The "Historic" Early IEC Ion Injection Experiment of R. Hirsch Working With Philo Farnsworth', is a labeled technical drawing of the apparatus showing a high-voltage dome containing auxiliary power supplies, high-voltage insulator, anode shell, viewing port, gas feed connector, ion gun, cathode, support insulator, and connection to pumps. Figure 2.2 is a log-scale graph of neutron output (neutrons/second, 10^5 to 10^10) versus applied potential (30-150 kV), with curves for 4.0 microns D-T and 0.1, 1.1, and 7.8 microns D2; the caption states DT rates exceeded 10^9 n/s at 150 kV.
